newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stocks end soft, sentiment negative.
newsitem.headline: S.African stocks end soft, sentiment negative.

text.p: South African shares ended softer on Wednesday continuing the weakness begun before the close on Tuesday when shares slid on a lower Wall Street opening.
Gold shares were softer, depressed by a dull bullion price which had slipped some $3 since Monday to trade around the $340 an ounce level.
Dealers said the market's performance on Wednesday had been disappointing given that Wall Street ended at a new high on Tuesday night, albeit on a slim 10 point rise, and the London bourse was firm.

But local factors, in particular poor results from two of South Africa's biggest retail and construction firms -- sectors which dealers said were good indicators of the country's level of economic activity -- weighed down stocks.
The 100 percent industrial index lost 65.1 points to 8,503.6 points, depressing the all-share index 51.2 points to 7,160.7. Gold index 23.0 points lower at 1,189.3.
